subject: AWS Marketplace private offer — activation latency, approvals & onboarding steps
message_1_subject: AWS Marketplace private offer — activation latency, approvals & onboarding steps
message_1_body:
Hi Alicia,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We discussed using an AWS Marketplace private offer (PO) so Acme Health can take advantage of consolidated billing while keeping billing and procurement familiar to your finance team. Two things I want to flag up-front that typically slow activation: buyer-approval latency (multiple sign-offs inside the buyer org) and cross-account entitlement mapping for our license keys.

To remove surprises, I attached an onboarding checklist and a short MPO activation matrix that outlines the typical handoffs, expected windows, and required artifacts from procurement/legal. High-level ask: can you confirm who in your org needs to sign the PO (name + role) and whether your procurement team requires invoice-first or PO-first activation? That will determine whether we should route via DocuSign or accept a PO as the activation trigger.

Attached: redwood_onboarding_checklist.pdf (technical steps + IAM role template), mpo_activation_matrix.xlsx ( approvals vs expected time).

If helpful I can loop in Karthik (pricing) and Priya (integrations) — they have quick answers for segmented entitlements and co-sell credits. Proposed next step: 30-minute call tomorrow to walk the activation matrix and confirm required artifacts.

Thanks,
Michael
Michael Grant

message_2_subject: Re: AWS Marketplace private offer — activation latency, approvals & onboarding steps
message_2_body:
Michael,

Appreciate the notes and the attachments — they help. Quick answers from our side:
- Approval chain: IT Security sign-off (Alicia Ramos), Procurement (Procurement Team alias), Legal (contract review). Final CFO signature rarely needed unless > $250k.
- Activation trigger: Our procurement group prefers PO-first activation for platform subscriptions (they create a PO, finance issues payment, then vendor activates). For pilots we sometimes allow invoice-first, but Procurement wants the PO on file for audit.

Procurement has two asks before they will generate the PO:
1) Confirmation of term length and if early-termination refunds are pro-rated (we usually ask for pro-rata refunds).
2) Evidence of SOC 2 and data isolation controls (we already have the vendor security questionnaire in progress).

Could you outline how Redwood handles activation if the buyer insists on PO-first (we need estimated time from PO submission to product activation in our systems)? Also, any guidance on whether a 12-month vs 24-month term affects internal approval lanes would be very helpful.

Looping in procurement@acmehealth.com to be explicit.

Thanks,
Alicia
Alicia Ramos
Dir. IT Security, Acme Health

message_3_subject: Re: AWS Marketplace private offer — activation latency, approvals & onboarding steps
message_3_body:
Hi Alicia and team,

Thanks for the details — quick answers from Redwood ops/finance side. I'm copying Karthik (pricing/discounts) and Priya (integrations) to cover the remaining points. Below is an actionable activation playbook for PO-first workflows: 

1) PO received by Redwood (procurement@redwood.com) -> Confirm business name match to Marketplace buyer account (T+0).
2) Finance validates PO terms vs private offer terms (T+0 to T+1 business day). If terms match, finance issues activation ticket to operations with the Marketplace private offer ID.
3) Ops performs entitlement mapping: create cross-account entitlement in AWS Marketplace, map license SKUs to Acme identities (T+1 to T+2 business days). This step requires the linked buyer AWS account ID and an IAM role template (attached).
4) Activation: once entitlements are mapped and Marketplace confirms acceptance, we flip the subscription to active on your side. Typical PO-first activation window: 1–3 business days assuming no contract redlines and buyer provides AWS account ID and PO that matches the offer ID.

A few additional notes:
- Term length: 12-month vs 24-month usually does not change the internal approval lane materially for Acme, but 24-month deals often require a slightly larger procurement review (they flagged anything > $500k historically). If you anticipate a 24-month term, Karthik can propose tiered pricing and an activation SLA credit.
- Early termination & refunds: our standard private-offer SOW includes pro-rated refunds for unused committed months unless an explicit non-refundable clause is negotiated. See redwood_sow_v1.pdf.
- SOC 2 & evidence: we can provide the SOC 2 Type 2 PDF and a short evidence packet (data retention, KMS use) — can share via secure link or with an NDA if needed.

Escrow/fallbacks for critical pilots: if Acme needs guaranteed shorter activation in future pilots, we can pre-stage entitlements for a single account (requires a one-time pre-provisioning form). This reduces activation to <24 hours but requires an upfront provisioning approval form.

Attachments: redwood_sow_v1.pdf (terms), redwood_onboarding_checklist.pdf (ops steps), mpo_activation_matrix.xlsx (detailed timelines).

Next step suggestion: Michael and I are available Thursday 09:00–12:00 PT to run a 30-minute activation walkthrough with Procurement and IT Security to confirm the PO template and required artifacts. If that works, Alicia — can you confirm a calendar invite?

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Dedicated Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0148
